Expectation1: Fix bugs and troubleshoot issues reported by users or QA
Situation1: Several users report intermittent errors that disrupt normal usage
Expectation2: Support individuals or groups in accessing essential services and resources
Situation2: They casually guide a youth, an older adult, or a refugee family toward available social or community services.
Story: I stared at my screen, the error logs piling up faster than I could read them. Users were frustrated, and QA was pinging me every hour for updates. As the lead developer, I was expected to fix these bugs immediately—every minute the system was down, more people were affected. My phone buzzed again, but this time it wasn’t work. It was a message from the community center: a refugee family I’d been helping needed urgent guidance to access housing services before the office closed. I felt the weight of both worlds pressing in. My team needed me to troubleshoot, to be the technical anchor. But the family needed me, too—someone to help them navigate a system they barely understood. I could hear the tension in my own breath, torn between the demands of code and compassion, knowing that whichever I chose, someone would be left waiting.
